title: September 25 Project Connect - Avondale
description:
### Event Description  
**Project Connect** is a one-stop resource event led by Keys to Change and designed to assist individuals who are experiencing or at risk of experiencing homelessness.  

This event brings together a wide range of service providers offering on-the-spot support, including:

- Housing or shelter access  
- Medicaid and nutrition assistance  
- Clothing and meals  
- Substance use treatment  
- Employment readiness services  
- Social Security assistance  
- Mental health support  
- And much more  

### Why Volunteers Are Needed  
Volunteers play a critical role in helping the event run smoothly and ensuring that guests feel welcomed, supported, and able to access the services they need.

### What You'll Be Doing  
By signing up, volunteers may assist with:

- Guest navigation and check-in  
- Distributing meals or supplies  
- Supporting service providers  
- Helping with event setup or teardown  
- Creating a warm, respectful environment for all attendees  

Your time and care can make a real difference in someone's life—thank you for showing up and serving our community!
accessibility_notes: Volunteers may be asked to work both indoors and outdoors in high temperatures (potentially exceeding 100°F). Air-conditioned breaks and rest opportunities will be provided throughout the day at your leisure. Please bring water and a snack and hydrate well the day and night prior. If you have any accessibility needs or require accommodations, please contact us in advance—we are happy to support and accommodate you.

description:
Most people know that having a Will is important. Still, many still don’t have one. But get this: Having just a Will is not enough! Mingle to learn estate planning basics and a little bit more.  This free public event is brought to you by [Sky Island Alliance](https://skyislandalliance.org/), [the Planned Giving Roundtable of Southern Arizona](https://www.pgrtsa.org/), and [Mission Management & Trust Co](https://missiontrust.com/). 

Attorney Jacquelyne J. Mingle: Jacque has been practicing in Tucson for more than a decade, and her practice encompasses a variety of elder law issues, including estate planning; estate and trust administration; and disputes over wills, trusts, and estates. She is a Fellow of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel, is one of U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Lawyers,” and is a Certified by the State Bar of Arizona as a Specialist in Estate and Trust Law. She is licensed as a fiduciary by the Arizona Supreme Court and served as chair of the State Bar’s Elder Law, Mental Health and Special Needs Planning Council and served on the Estate & Trust Law Advisory Commission for the State Bar’s Board of Legal Specialization. She also serves on the Boards of Directors for the Southern Arizona Estate Planning Council and Tohono Chul Park. Jacque’s J.D. is from the U of A’s James E. Rogers College of Law, where she has taught the Trusts & Estates course as an adjunct professor. Before becoming an attorney, Jacque was an editor at USA Today supervising entertainment coverage. She did her undergraduate work at the University of Kansas and roots for both the Jayhawks (Rock Chalk!) and the Wildcats (Bear Down!).

title: Bystander Intervention De-escalation Training presented by SURJ MKE
description:
Now more than ever, it’s going to take community to keep each other safe and minimize harm. No one is born with these skills, it takes lifelong learning and practice to keep the tools in your harm reduction toolbox sharp. Whether you’ve attended workshops before or this is your first time, this is the space for you!

Bystander Intervention/De-escalation training will focus on ways to intervene in public instances of racist, sexist, anti-Muslim, anti-Semitic, anti-Trans, and other forms of oppressive interpersonal violence and harassment while considering the safety of all parties. The physical and vocal practice of various strategies is designed to change social norms and encourage people to find ways to interrupt violence and prevent further harm.

This workshop includes a learning segment of tips and strategies, how to document, knowing your rights as an intervener, and practice scenarios constructed on ways to show up and support a diversity of identities through an intersectional lenses, both as the intervener and the person experiencing harm.
